note: Four stages, each tied to a real step of the checker. Clip seconds are measured against media/master.mp4 as built by scripts/build_flight.py, not planned. Change the master and this file has to change with it; the tests check the two agree.

beats.why: The first frame holds still while the claim input and the skip link are read and used. Nothing moves until the reader chooses to scroll.
The claim arrives the way it really arrives: at night, on a phone, with no source attached. focusX left of centre on mobile because the phone sits left of frame.
The longest beat. It carries the real PubMed query, the counter climbing to eight, and eight real study cards stacking in, so it needs the most scroll distance of any stage.
Each card takes its grade from evidence.py and the stack sorts, strongest at the bottom. Long enough to watch the order change rather than see it jump.
The footage drains into the deep field. The cards compress into the evidence bar and the claim shrinks away. Short: this is a transition, not a reading beat.
Holds on the deep field while the verdict, the still-open card and the claim input are read. hold -1 means the last frame, which is the flat deep field the section below continues.

chapters.ch-claim: Heard a health claim? Check it against the research.
chapters.ch-search: We search the published research, not the internet.
chapters.ch-grade: Each study graded by what kind of evidence it is.
chapters.ch-verdict: Likely true. Likely false. It's complicated.
chapters.ch-open: And every verdict says what is still open.
